segmentation: The segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of entities across the five frames of the multi-level construction site, localizing the lower worker ('person') at roughly 0.5–1.5 m below the camera wearer in frame 1 and again in the upper-right of frame 5 at about 0.5–1.5 m distance as the camera pans down and left. While the RGB context shows the worker facing forward/left toward his buckets and looking down toward the elevated camera wearer, and shows a second person's pink-sleeved arm partially occluded under the upper ledge in frame 4 about 0.5–1.5 m below, the segmentation masks only provide 2D silhouettes that shift from center-right (frame 1) to absent (frames 2–4, including when the wall occludes the scene in frame 3) to upper-right and center-left (frame 5). Compared to the busy RGB image, the masks sharply isolate the silhouette of the worker and the circular pan from the crosshatched bamboo poles and shadows, but the map is highly unreliable: it misses the worker entirely in frames 2 and 4, misses the large background pan at the bottom of frames 4 and 5 (3–5 m from the wearer and out of reach), and mislabels the wearer's trowel/hand in frame 1 as 'cat' and the mortar pan in frame 5 as 'toilet'.
pose: The pose map extracts 2D yellow body skeletons for the worker located about 0.5–1.5 m below the camera wearer in frames 1 and 2, while remained completely blank in frames 3, 4, and 5 and detecting no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frames 1 and 2, the keypoints trace the worker's head, torso, and outstretched arms from an overhead angle, showing his torso oriented toward the lower-left of the image with both arms extended 3–5 m forward to grasp and tilt the cement bucket over the round pan out of his arm's reach, while his head is angled downward toward the camera wearer. From frame 1 to frame 2, as the camera tilts slightly upward and right toward the distant wall, the detected skeleton shifts toward the bottom-right corner of the frame and elongates as the worker leans further over the pan, with his lower legs occluded and cropped at the bottom edge of frame 2. This skeletal wireframe clarifies the overhead orientation of the worker's shoulders, elbows, and head through the cluttered bamboo shadows better than the RGB image alone, but it is unreliable under extreme top-down foreshortening—compressing the torso into a box-like shape, failing to detect the worker's hands or the camera wearer's own hand 3–5 m away and out of reach in frame 1, and failing to detect the worker in frames 4 and 5 when he is partially occluded or seen from the front and above.
